question: ADF equipment in the aircraft is used in conjunction with which ground-based system?
explanation: The text states that Automatic Direction Finder (ADF) equipment in the aircraft is used in conjunction with a simple low and medium frequency non-directional beacon (NDB) on the ground.

question: The Non-directional Beacon (NDB) transmits which type of radio signals?

options.text: Horizontally polarized signals in all directions
Vertically polarized signals in all directions
Circularly polarized signals in one direction
Elliptically polarized signals in all directions

explanation: The text states that the Non-directional Beacon (NDB) is a ground based transmitter which transmits vertically polarized radio signals, in all directions (hence the name).

question: NDBs transmit in which frequency bands?
explanation: The text states that NDBs transmit in the Low Frequency (LF) and Medium Frequency (MF) bands.

question: A 'cone of silence' exists overhead the NDB transmitter during which:

options.text: The aircraft does not receive any signals
The aircraft receives only sky wave signals
The aircraft receives only surface wave signals

explanation: The text states that a 'cone of silence' exists overhead the NDB transmitter during which the aircraft does not receive any signals. The diameter of the cone increases with aircraft height.

question: The ADF measures the bearing of an NDB relative to:

options.text: The fore/aft axis of the aircraft
The lateral axis of the aircraft

explanation: The text states that the ADF measures the bearing of an NDB relative to the fore/aft axis of the aircraft.

question: The polar diagram formed by a loop aerial is:
explanation: The text states that the polar diagram formed is a figure of eight as shown below (Figure 7.2). It can be seen that there are two null positions.

question: To resolve the 180° ambiguity of the loop aerial, a simple dipole aerial called a sense aerial is added. Its polar diagram is:
explanation: The text states that to resolve this ambiguity a simple dipole aerial, called a sense aerial, is added. The polar diagram of the sense aerial is circular.

question: When the field from the sense aerial is combined with the loop aerial, the resultant polar diagram is known as a:
explanation: The text states that the resultant polar diagram is known as a CARDIOID. The cardioid has a single null.

question: To improve the accuracy to meet the ICAO requirement, the polarity of the sense aerial is reversed to produce a right hand cardioid and then rapidly switching between the two cardioids at about:
explanation: The text states that the polarity of the sense aerial is reversed to produce a right hand cardioid. Then by rapidly switching (about 120 Hz) between the two cardioids, the null is more precisely defined and hence the accuracy is improved.

question: The ICAO accuracy requirement for ADF is:
explanation: The text states that the resultant null with a single cardioid is not precise enough to meet the ICAO accuracy requirement of +/-5°.

question: In reality, the loop is fixed and has how many elements?
explanation: The text states that in reality it is not feasible to have a rotating loop outside the aircraft, so the loop is fixed and has four elements, two aligned with the fore-aft axis of the aircraft with the other two perpendicular to the fore-aft axis.

question: The device that reproduces the electromagnetic field detected by the fixed loop aerial is called a:
explanation: The text states that the electrical fields are transmitted to a similar four elements in a goniometer reproducing the electro magnetic field detected by the aerial.

question: The allocated frequencies for NDBs are:
explanation: The text states that the allocated frequencies for NDBs are 190 - 1750 kHz in the LF and MF bands.

question: Most NDBs will be found between about:
explanation: The text states that since the mode of propagation used is surface wave, most NDBs will be found between about 250 and 450 kHz.

question: A Locator (L) NDB is a low powered NDB used for airfield or runway approach procedures and normally has a range of:
explanation: The text states that Locator (L) are low powered NDBs used for airfield or runway approach procedures. They normally have ranges of 10 to 25 NM.

question: En route NDBs have a range of:
explanation: The text states that En route NDBs have a range of 50 NM or more, and where serving oceanic areas may have ranges of several hundred miles.

question: The aircraft ADF equipment comprises:

options.text: A loop aerial, a sense aerial, a control unit, a receiver and a display
A loop aerial, a control unit and a display only
A sense aerial, a receiver and a display only
A loop aerial, a sense aerial and a display only

explanation: The text states that the aircraft equipment comprises: A loop aerial, A sense aerial, A control unit, A receiver, A display.

question: The emission designator N0NA1A indicates:
explanation: The text states that the A1A part is the emission of an interrupted unmodulated carrier wave which requires the BFO to be on for aural reception.

question: For N0NA1A beacons, the BFO should be selected:

options.text: ON for tuning, identification and monitoring
OFF for tuning, identification and monitoring
ON for tuning and OFF for identification

explanation: The text states that when using N0NA1A beacons, the BFO should be selected ON for (manual) tuning, identification and monitoring.

question: For N0NA2A beacons, the BFO should be selected:

options.text: ON for tuning, identification and monitoring
ON for tuning but OFF for identification and monitoring
OFF for tuning and ON for identification
OFF for tuning, identification and monitoring

explanation: The text states that N0NA2A beacons require the BFO ON for (manual) tuning but OFF for identification and monitoring.

question: ADF information may be presented on:

options.text: Either an RBI or an RMI

explanation: The text states that the information may be presented on a relative bearing indicator (RBI) or a radio magnetic indicator (RMI).

question: The RBI has a standard compass rose where 360° is aligned with:

options.text: The fore-aft axis of the aircraft
The lateral axis of the aircraft

explanation: The text states that the RBI has a standard compass rose where 360° is aligned with the fore-aft axis of the aircraft.

question: The needle of an ADF indicator always points to the beacon (QDM) and the tail of the needle gives the:
explanation: The text states that the needle always points to the beacon (QDM) and the tail of the needle gives the QDR.

question: Which of the following is NOT a use of the NDB?

options.text: Homing to or flying from the NDB
Holding overhead at an assigned level in a race-track pattern

explanation: The text lists the uses of the NDB as: En route navigational bearings, Homing to or flying from the NDB when maintaining airway centre lines, Holding overhead at an assigned level in a race-track pattern, and Runway instrument approach procedures. NDB provides non-precision approaches, not precision approach guidance.

question: Homing to an NDB in zero wind means:

options.text: Maintaining a constant relative bearing of 360°
Maintaining a constant relative bearing of 180°

explanation: The text states that Figure 7.10 shows an aircraft maintaining 360° relative bearing, in zero wind (zero drift). The aircraft is heading 077° and therefore will track inbound on 077°.

question: Homing to an NDB with a crosswind and making no allowance for drift will result in:

options.text: A straight track to the beacon
A curved track to the beacon
A track that oscillates around the required track

explanation: The text states that Figure 7.11 shows an aircraft maintaining a relative bearing of 360°, with a crosswind from the left. As a result a curved track will be followed.

question: To track inbound to an NDB with a crosswind, the correct method is to:

options.text: Maintain a constant relative bearing of 360°
Allow for the anticipated drift therefore maintaining a constant track
Fly directly towards the beacon without drift correction

explanation: The text states that to achieve a required track inbound to an NDB, with a crosswind, the correct method is to allow for the anticipated drift therefore maintaining a constant track.

question: For 20° starboard drift inbound to an NDB on a track of 080°, the heading should be:
explanation: The text states that in Figure 7.12, 20° Starboard drift is anticipated, so 20 is Subtracted from track. The aircraft is heading 060° with a relative bearing of 020°.

question: For 28° port drift inbound to an NDB on a track of 080°, the heading should be:
explanation: The text states that in Figure 7.13, 28° Port drift is anticipated, so this is added (Plus) to the track value. The aircraft is heading 108° with a relative bearing of 332°.

question: In Figure 7.14, an aircraft maintaining the required track outbound from an NDB in zero wind is heading 260° and has a relative bearing of:
explanation: The text states that Figure 7.14 shows an aircraft maintaining the required track outbound from an NDB in zero wind (zero drift) conditions. The aircraft is heading 260° and has a relative bearing of 180°.

question: An aircraft maintaining a track of 100° outbound from an NDB with 23° starboard drift will have a heading of:
explanation: The text states that in Figure 7.15, 23° of Starboard drift is anticipated, this is Subtracted from the track, therefore the heading is 077° with a relative bearing of 203° from the NDB.

question: To assess drift outbound from an NDB, the aircraft must:

options.text: Maintain a steady heading from directly overhead the beacon

explanation: The text states that to assess drift by this means the aircraft must maintain a steady heading from directly overhead the beacon.

question: In a holding pattern, each aircraft is separated vertically from other aircraft by a minimum of:
explanation: The text states that the area, also known as a 'stack', is organized over a 'radio' beacon where each waiting aircraft flies a special circuit separated vertically from other aircraft by a minimum of 1000 ft.

question: The DOC of NDBs is based upon a daytime protection ratio (signal/noise ratio) of:
explanation: The text states that the DOC of NDBs is based upon a daytime protection ratio (signal/noise ratio of 3:1) between wanted and unwanted signals that permits the required level of bearing accuracy.

question: Precipitation static is generated by:

options.text: The collision of water droplets and ice crystals with the aircraft

explanation: The text states that precipitation static is generated by the collision of water droplets and ice crystals with the aircraft.

question: The indications on the RMI/RBI when precipitation static is present will be:

options.text: A steady needle and clear audio
A wandering needle and background hiss on the audio
A needle pointing to the Cb

explanation: The text states that the indications on the RMI/RBI will be a wandering needle and the audio will have a background hiss, which is also likely to be present on VHF frequencies.

question: A static discharge in a cumulonimbus cloud (Cb) will be heard as a loud crackle on the audio and the needle will:

options.text: Move rapidly to point to the Cb

explanation: The text states that a static discharge in a cumulonimbus cloud (Cb) will be heard as a loud crackle on the audio and the needle will move rapidly to point to the Cb.

question: Night effect is caused by:

options.text: The D-region absorbing signals in the LF and MF bands
The D-region disappearing at night allowing sky wave contamination of the surface wave
The E-region absorbing signals in the LF and MF bands

explanation: The text states that by day the D-region absorbs signals in the LF and MF bands. At night the D-region disappears allowing sky wave contamination of the surface wave being used.

question: Night effect first becomes significant at what range from the NDB?
explanation: The text states that the effect first becomes significant at 70 - 100 NM from the NDB.

question: Night effect is worst around:
explanation: The text states that the effect is manifest by fading of the audio signal and the needle 'hunting' and is worst around dawn and dusk, when the ionosphere is in transition.

question: When using ADF at night, which of the following precautions should be taken?

options.text: Avoid use of the equipment within 1 hour of sunrise or sunset
Use only NDBs beyond their promulgated range
Ignore the needle if it wanders
Use the equipment only below 5000 ft

explanation: The text states that if ADF is to be used at night: Positively identify the NDB call sign, Continue to check the tuning and the identification, Avoid use of the equipment within 1 hour of sunrise or sunset, Use NDBs within their promulgated range which is valid during daytime only, Treat bearings with caution if the needle wanders and the signal fades, Cross-check NDB bearing information against other navigation aids.

question: Station interference at night can be expected:

options.text: Even within the DOC because of sky wave contamination from stations out of range by day

explanation: The text states that at night, one can expect interference even within the DOC because of sky wave contamination from stations out of range by day.

question: Mountain effect on ADF bearings can be minimized by:
explanation: The text states that mountainous areas can cause reflections and diffraction of the transmitted radio waves to produce errors in ADF systems. These errors will increase at low altitude and can be minimized by flying higher.

question: Coastal refraction is negligible when the angle of incidence is:
explanation: The text states that refraction is negligible at 90° to the coast but increases as the angle of incidence increases.

question: For an aircraft flying over the sea, coastal refraction puts the aircraft position:

options.text: Further from the coast than its actual position
Closer to the coast than its actual position

explanation: The text states that for an aircraft flying over the sea the error puts the aircraft position closer to the coast than its actual position.

question: The effect of coastal refraction can be minimized by:

options.text: Using NDBs on or near to the coast
Using signals that cross the coast at acute angles

explanation: The text states that the effect can be minimised by: Using NDBs on or near to the coast, Flying higher, Using signals that cross the coast at or near to 90°.

question: Quadrantal error is caused by:

options.text: The airframe producing a strong electrical field aligned fore and aft
Static build up on the airframe

explanation: The text states that the theoretical reception polar diagram of the loop aerial is distorted by the airframe which produces a strong electrical field aligned fore and aft. Incoming NDB signals are thus refracted towards the fore and aft airframe axis.

question: The maximum quadrantal error occurs on relative bearings of:
explanation: The text states that the maximum refraction occurs in the quadrants (i.e. on relative bearings of 045°, 135°, 225° & 315°).

question: Angle of bank (dip) error is only present when:

options.text: The aircraft is in level flight
The aircraft is not in level flight
The aircraft is on the ground
The aircraft is flying straight and level

explanation: The text states that this error is only present when the aircraft is not in level flight.

question: Lack of failure warning system in ADF means:

options.text: False indications due to a failure are readily detectable
False indications due to a failure are not readily detectable
The system automatically switches to standby
The needle points to the failure

explanation: The text states that false indications due to a failure in the system are not readily detectable because of the absence of failure warning on most ADF instruments.

question: The range of NDB/ADF equipment is proportional to:

options.text: The square root of the power output
The square of the power output
The inverse of the power output

explanation: The text states that NDB transmission power; the range is proportional to the square root of the power output i.e. to double the NDB range, quadruple the power output of the transmitter.

question: NDB range over water is calculated as:
explanation: The text states that NDB range is greater over water: 3 × √P (W) over water.

question: NDB range over land is calculated as:
explanation: The text states that NDB range is greater over water: 2 × √P (W) over land.

question: Which type of NDB has greater ranges?
explanation: The text states that N0NA1A NDBs have greater ranges than N0NA2A. But note that ICAO Annex 10 recommends the use of N0NA2A for long range beacons.

question: The accuracy of ADF is +/-5° within the designated operational coverage:
explanation: The text states that the accuracy of ADF is +/-5° within the designated operational coverage, by day only. This refers to the measured bearing and does not include any compass error.

question: The phenomenon of coastal refraction which affects the accuracy of ADF bearings:

options.text: Can be minimized by using beacons situated well inland
Can be minimized by taking bearings where the signal crosses the coastline at right angles
Is most marked one hour before to one hour after sunrise and sunset

explanation: The text states that the effect can be minimised by using signals that cross the coast at or near to 90°.

question: An aircraft is intending to track from NDB 'A' to NDB 'B' on a track of 050°(T), heading 060°(T). If the RBI shows the relative bearing of 'A' to be 180° and the relative bearing of 'B' to be 330° then the aircraft is:
explanation: The relative bearing of 'A' is 180° (directly behind), meaning the aircraft has passed 'A'. The relative bearing of 'B' is 330° (30° left of the nose), meaning 'B' is ahead and to the left. Since the aircraft is heading 060° and tracking 050°, the aircraft is starboard of track and nearer 'B'.

question: ADF quadrantal error is caused by:

options.text: Static build up on the airframe and St. Elmo's Fire
The aircraft's major electrical axis, the fuselage, reflecting and re-radiating the incoming NDB transmissions
NDB signals speeding up and bending as they cross from a land to water propagation path

explanation: The text states that the theoretical reception polar diagram of the loop aerial is distorted by the airframe which produces a strong electrical field aligned fore and aft. Incoming NDB signals are thus refracted towards the fore and aft airframe axis.

question: The overall accuracy of ADF bearings by day within the promulgated range (DOC) is:
explanation: The text states that the accuracy of ADF is +/-5° within the designated operational coverage, by day only.

question: In order to Tune, Identify and Monitor N0NA1A NDB emissions the BFO should be used as follows:

options.text: Tune: On, Identify: On, Monitor: Off
Tune: On, Identify: On, Monitor: On
Tune: On, Identify: Off, Monitor: Off
Tune: Off, Identify: Off, Monitor: Off

explanation: The text states that when using N0NA1A beacons, the BFO should be selected ON for (manual) tuning, identification and monitoring.

question: The magnitude of the error in position lines derived from ADF bearings that are affected by coastal refraction may be reduced by:

options.text: Only using beacons within the designated operational coverage
Choosing beacons on or near the coast

explanation: The text states that the effect can be minimised by: Using NDBs on or near to the coast, Flying higher, Using signals that cross the coast at or near to 90°.

question: The BFO facility on ADF equipment should be used as follows when an NDB having N0NA1A type emission is to be used:

options.text: BFO on for tuning and identification but may be turned off for monitoring
BFO on for tuning but can be turned off for monitoring and identification purpose
BFO off during tuning, identification and monitoring because this type of emission is not modulated
BFO should be switched on for tuning, ident and monitoring

explanation: The text states that when using N0NA1A beacons, the BFO should be selected ON for (manual) tuning, identification and monitoring.

question: The protection ratio of 3:1 that is provided within the promulgated range/designated operational coverage of an NDB by day cannot be guaranteed at night because of:

options.text: Long range sky wave interference from other transmitters
Sky wave signals from the NDB to which you are tuned
The increased skip distance that occurs at night
The possibility of sporadic E returns occurring at night

explanation: The text states that at night, one can expect interference even within the DOC because of sky wave contamination from stations out of range by day.

question: Each NDB has a range promulgated in the COMM section of the AIP. Within this range interference from other NDBs should not cause bearing errors in excess of:
explanation: The text states that the accuracy of ADF is +/-5° within the designated operational coverage, by day only.

question: The range promulgated in the AIP and flight guides for all NDBs in the UK is the range:

options.text: Within which a protection ratio of 3:1 is guaranteed by day and night
Up to which bearings can be obtained on 95% of occasions
Within which bearings obtained by day should be accurate to within 5°
Within which protection from sky wave protection is guaranteed

explanation: The text states that the accuracy of ADF is +/-5° within the designated operational coverage, by day only.

question: In order to resolve the 180° directional ambiguity of a directional LOOP aerial its polar diagram is combined with that of a SENSE aerial ...... to produce a ...... whose single null ensures the ADF needle moves the shortest distance to indicate the correct ......
explanation: The text states that to resolve this ambiguity a simple dipole aerial, called a sense aerial, is added. The resultant polar diagram is known as a CARDIOID. The cardioid has a single null which ensures the ADF needle moves the shortest distance to indicate the correct bearing.

question: The protection ratio afforded to NDBs in the UK within the promulgated range (DOC) applies:
explanation: The text states that the accuracy of ADF is +/-5° within the designated operational coverage, by day only.

question: The phenomena of coastal refraction affecting ADF bearings is caused by the signal ...... when it reaches the coastline and bending ...... the normal to the coast:
explanation: The text states that radio waves speed up over water due to the reduced absorption of energy (attenuation) compared to that which occurs over land. This speeding up causes the wave front to bend (refract) away from its normal path and pull it towards the coast.

question: In an ADF system, night effect is most pronounced:

options.text: When the aircraft is at low altitude
When the aircraft is at high altitude

explanation: The text states that the effect is manifest by fading of the audio signal and the needle 'hunting' and is worst around dawn and dusk, when the ionosphere is in transition.

question: When the induced signals from the loop and the sense antenna are combined in an ADF receiver, the resultant polar diagram is:
explanation: The text states that the resultant polar diagram is known as a CARDIOID.

question: When flying over the sea and using an inland NDB to fix position with a series of position lines, the plotted position in relation to the aircraft's actual position will be:

options.text: Inaccurate due to the transmitted wave front decelerating

explanation: The text states that for an aircraft flying over the sea the error puts the aircraft position closer to the coast than its actual position.

question: An aircraft on a heading of 235°(M) shows an RMI reading of 090° with respect to an NDB. Any quadrantal error which is affecting the accuracy of this bearing is likely to be:

options.text: Zero, since quadrantal error affects only the RBI
Zero, since quadrantal error affects only the VOR

explanation: The text states that the maximum refraction occurs in the quadrants (i.e. on relative bearings of 045°, 135°, 225° & 315°). The relative bearing is 090°, which is in the quadrant, so the error is likely to be a maximum value.

question: The principal propagation path employed in an NDB/ADF system is:
explanation: The text states that since the mode of propagation used is surface wave, most NDBs will be found between about 250 and 450 kHz.

question: The ADF of an aircraft on a heading of 189°(T) will experience the greatest effect due to quadrantal error if the NDB bears:
explanation: The relative bearing = 234° - 189° = 45°. The maximum refraction occurs on relative bearings of 045°, 135°, 225° & 315°. Since the relative bearing is 45°, this is a maximum error position.
